printed_headline_estimate: COVID-19 perception vs. sanitation service provision perception: Pearson chi-square p <= 0.001, r = 0.1149 (Table 2, PDF p. 10, N = 449); COVID-19 perception vs. water service provision perception: Pearson chi-square p <= 0.014, r = -0.1194 (Table 5, PDF pp. 12-13, N = 449); COVID-19 perception vs. need for governance change: Pearson chi-square p <= 0.001 (Table 8, PDF p. 15, N = 449).
publication_year_note: The printed journal issue header on every page (PDF pp. 1-19) states 'African Journal of Governance and Development | Volume 14 Issue 1 • July • 2025' (verified publication year 2025). Note that the DOI string printed on PDF p. 1 ('https://doi.org/10.36369/2616-9045/2024/v14i1a4') contains '2024', while Tables 1-8 cite 'Survey Data (2024)' and PDF p. 17 cites a source dated '10 December 2024'.
rationale: Although the study reports inferential bivariate Pearson chi-square p-values and correlation coefficients (r) across N = 449 surveyed households in Lepelle-Nkumpi Local Municipality, no tested exposure-outcome pair satisfies SWiM eligibility. Tables 2 and 5 cross-tabulate respondents' 5-point Likert perceptions of 'COVID-19' against their Likert perceptions of municipal sanitation provision (p <= 0.001, r = 0.1149) and water provision (p <= 0.014, r = -0.1194). This fails narrow Criterion 2 because the tested exposure ('COVID-19' pandemic shock/perception in a single cross-sectional survey within one municipality) is an exogenous public-health disaster rather than variation in a rule-type legal, tenure, tariff, regulatory, administrative, or ownership mechanism. Conversely, Tables 6-8 ('Financial resources', 'ICT', and respondent opinion on 'the need for municipal governance to change') test bivariate associations with 'COVID-19' rather than a household water or sanitation service access outcome (failing both Criterion 2 and Criterion 4).
